According to Adam Smith, division of labour increases productivity in several key ways:

1. **Reduces the time required for each individual to produce the same quantity of goods**. When one part of the labour is specialised in producing a particular kind of good, it becomes more efficient than when the whole labour is divided among different specialised parts.
